chunks: Not only do they not believe in God, but also associate others with Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between general belief and true faith in Islam according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (12:106) is often interpreted to distinguish between the majority's nominal belief and the exclusive, unwavering faith of the Imams and prophets, who remained free from subtle Shirk. It underscores the concept that true Tawhid requires not just verbal affirmation but a purity of heart and practice, a theme central to the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt. This critique of superficial faith serves as a reminder that many believers may still associate partners with God through idolatry of status, wealth, or self.
